fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is MoS2 addition, whereas the target intervention varies Mo content in an already formulated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.

It incorrectly treats an MoS2 tribofilm as thermally stable and operative throughout air sliding to 800 °C; the high-temperature mechanism instead depends on oxidation and formation of compact oxide/silver-molybdate glazes.
It predicts consistently lower friction and wear at every temperature, which is unsupported and misses the severe intermediate-temperature wear maximum.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
Critical test parameters—including the specified 8 N load, counterface, speed, distance, and discrete temperatures—are absent.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of reducing friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C and proposes a controlled comparison with wear-track analysis. However, it does not reconstruct the studied material or intervention: MoS2 was already one constituent of a Ni-coated MoS2/Ag/Cr2O3 composite, while Mo concentration in the HEA matrix was the varied factor. Its single-film mechanism is credible mainly at lower temperatures and does not capture Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, thermal softening at 200–400 °C, or high-temperature silver-molybdate/oxide glaze formation. The generic unmodified-CoCrFeNi baseline also prevents direct comparison with the relevant Mo0.2 composite. Although the experiment could test the alternative hypothesis, its lack of fixed tribological conditions, phase controls, and cited evidence makes the full-range claim unsupported.
